item.title: Eminem Brings Back Slim Shady To Wreck His Spotify Awards
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Eminem's animated alter ego turns Spotify's Billions Club celebration into a roast and smashes plaques for his biggest hits.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem brought Slim Shady back to wreck his own awards in Spotify’s new Billions Club special. The Detroit rapper gets a pile of plaques for some of his biggest songs, then watches his animated alter ego make a sport of destroying them.

“The Real Slim Shady has entered the Billions Club, and he has the plaques to prove it,” Spotify wrote on X in the launch post. Its caption directs listeners to the full episode, “now on Spotify.”

The short opens with Mom’s Spaghetti served on the plaque for “Lose Yourself,” a nod to the song that put the dish in Eminem’s lyrics.

Shady emerges from the spaghetti and pulls Eminem into the cartoon with him. In the short, a chainsaw takes care of “Not Afraid,” while Shady sends the plaques for both Rihanna collaborations, “Love the Way You Lie” and “The Monster,” flying with a catapult.

Even “The Real Slim Shady” doesn’t get a pass. Shady puts that plaque and the one for “Without Me” under a guillotine after taking a shot at how similar the songs are.

Another plaque belongs to “Smack That,” the Akon single that also earned a diamond certification in the United States this month. That award recognizes sales and streams under the RIAA’s rules, while the plaque in the short is for Spotify streams alone.

Spotify hands out the plaques when individual songs reach a billion streams on the service.

Episodes typically give artists room to look back on how their biggest songs came together. Eminem uses his turn to let the character behind some of those hits tear into them.

The pair have been at each other before. Eminem made that fight the premise of his 2024 concept album The Death of Slim Shady (Coup De Grâce), then sat opposite his younger alter ego for a face-off.

In that video, the two had words. This time Shady takes it out on the hardware.

item.title: GTA VI Downloads Break Comcast Record Before Launch
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: GTA VI downloads set a Comcast record before launch. Here's how Fastly fits in and how Xfinity customers can claim a speed boost.
item.content:encoded:
Comcast says Grand Theft Auto VI drove the biggest single traffic event in its network’s history before players could even get into Vice City.

The rush to download the game ahead of its Thursday launch pushed Comcast to its third-busiest day ever. Traffic that day topped this year’s Super Bowl, according to Comcast Chief Network Officer Elad Nafshi.

Xbox downloads started rolling in Monday evening, followed by PlayStation downloads overnight. Comcast said in its account of the first 48 hours that gaming traffic nearly doubled from its usual level once PlayStation preloads began. Comcast put the size of the game download at roughly 212 gigabytes.

Now Comcast is working with Fastly to bring big game downloads closer to players. The companies can store copies of popular game files inside Comcast’s network instead of pulling each copy from farther away.

In a joint announcement, the companies said the approach can cut the time it takes data to make a round trip by more than 40 percent. They previously used the same approach to help Peacock stream major live sports.

“Grand Theft Auto VI could be one of the biggest moments in Internet history,” Nafshi said in the announcement.

The launch also brings a free 15-day speed boost of up to 2 gigabits per second for eligible Xfinity Internet customers. Comcast said customers can claim it through December 3 in the Xfinity app or on the Xfinity Membership page. If the offer doesn’t show up, the company says to contact customer service to request access.

“Millions of people are going to hit download the moment Grand Theft Auto VI becomes available,” Comcast marketing executive Kohposh Kuda said when the company announced the offer.

Rockstar’s long-awaited return to Vice City arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with Miami rap woven into its version of South Florida. Trick Daddy and Trina host Dirty South Classics, an in-game station built around Southern rap.

The music rollout extends beyond the console. Rockstar and Atlantic Records set the game’s 34-track companion album for the same day, with a Miami launch festival featuring Cardi B to follow on Saturday.

item.title: Yella Beezy Sent To Texas Prison Farm After MO3 Murder Conviction
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Yella Beezy's reported move puts him at Ramsey, a Texas prison with farm operations, as his lawyers prepare an appeal.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy is now serving his life sentence at a Texas prison farm south of Houston, according to a report identifying his new placement at the Ramsey Unit.

The rapper’s move to the W.F. Ramsey Unit in Rosharon appears in state prison records, according to FOX 26 Houston. The station cited the Texas Department of Criminal Justice in its report.

The Houston-area placement follows his conviction in Dallas County, where prosecutors pursued a murder-for-hire case over the highway shooting that killed MO3.

The Texas Department of Criminal Justice lists Ramsey in Brazoria County, with room for 1,865 men. Its custody classifications cover several levels, including security detention and outside trusty assignments.

Ramsey shares agricultural operations with the Stringfellow and Terrell units. Those operations include a cotton gin, cattle and swine programs, crops and a vegetable cannery. The department also lists a furniture-refinishing factory at Ramsey.

The three units occupy a shared site covering approximately 14,667 acres, with another 2,200 acres leased, according to the department’s directory.

Ramsey also offers education through Alvin Community College and the University of Houston-Clear Lake, which lists bachelor’s and master’s degrees. The directory identifies literacy and high-school-equivalency instruction, plus automotive training and cabinetmaking, among the options available at the unit.

Yella Beezy entered state custody after a Dallas County jury convicted him on November 11. He received life without parole for arranging and financing the attack that killed MO3 six years earlier.

MO3 was driving on Interstate 35E when a gunman confronted him. He abandoned his vehicle and tried to run away, but the shooter pursued him and opened fire on the highway. Another person wounded during the attack survived.

The defense is preparing to challenge the result. Attorney Toby Shook announced plans to appeal after the verdict, disputing whether prosecutors proved their case beyond a reasonable doubt.

“We’re going to keep fighting. We have excellent appellate points and that will be the next step in the fight,” Shook said.

His team’s trial challenges included the prosecution’s cash-payment theory and testimony about an alleged confession, disputes the jury ultimately resolved against the rapper.

Gunman Kewon White was separately convicted in September and also sentenced to life without parole.

Ramsey opened in July 1908.

item.title: TikTok Says 94% Of Global 200 Entries Went Viral Before Charting
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: TikTok commissions new research on music discovery as artists and labels wrestle with the pressure to produce viral songs.
item.content:encoded:
TikTok is backing its pitch to the music industry with new numbers: its commissioned study says 94% of the sampled 2025 Billboard Global 200 entries went viral on the app before charting.

The platform commissioned Luminate to prepare its 2026 Music Impact Report. Its findings arrive as artists including Tricky question how labels use viral success to decide whose career gets investment.

The report announcement also describes a correlation between TikTok views and streaming growth. Across 516 artists, 43% showed a strong or moderate positive relationship between views and on-demand audio streams in 2025.

That measures movement between the two figures, rather than establishing that TikTok caused the streaming gains.

The chart sample covered 484 songs between March 11 and December 4, 2025, excluding Christmas and holiday releases, according to Music Business Worldwide.

“Our community doesn’t just discover music. It helps turn songs into hits and connects fans with the music they go on to stream and buy,” said Tracy Gardner, TikTok’s global head of music business development.

Tricky has criticized labels chasing TikTok hits, describing a business that signs an artist around one viral record and loses interest when the follow-up fails. He prefers completing an album before choosing its singles.

For his own work, that can mean leaving a potentially radio-friendly track off a project when it does not fit. His song “Out of Place” reached BBC 6 Music’s A-list despite advice against making it a single.

The track had no chorus. Tricky released his 2013 album through his own False Idols label after making two albums for Domino. In Under the Radar, he credited greater creative control with renewing his interest in recording, including the ability to make mixing decisions without seeking permission from a label.

TikTok is also building direct relationships with established artists through SoundOn. Daddy Yankee released the 15-track La Postal through DY Records in partnership with the service on October 30.

The arrangement included worldwide distribution, artist services and promotion. TikTok created an album hub and search experience, with tasks that unlocked a profile frame and exclusive video content.

La Postal features Cardi B, Myke Towers, Danny Ocean, Bizarrap and Diljit Dosanjh.

item.title: Zane Lowe Says Jay-Z Changed His Approach To Artist Interviews
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Zane Lowe recalls the conversation that loosened radio's grip on his interview style and gave artists more room to talk.
item.content:encoded:
Zane Lowe credits Jay-Z with helping him rethink interviews, trading radio’s pressure to keep listeners tuned in for a conversation with room to breathe.

Speaking with Kristin Robinson on Billboard’s On The Record, the Apple Music executive recalled the rapper insisting on a longer format.

“It was the Jay-Z interview, which he insisted we make long form,” Lowe said.

YouTube helped change his priorities. Rather than concentrating on what made effective radio, he could return to an open-ended exchange.

Lowe also reflected on gifted musicians whose careers suffered because they chose the wrong business partners. His examples included managers, record companies, lawyers and publicists.

His frustration with the business hasn’t spoiled the music itself. “I never get jaded by music. The listening of it, the playing it,” Lowe said.

The earlier Jay-Z conversation shows how much ground that approach could cover. While discussing Magna Carta Holy Grail, the rapper explained how his relationship with Timbaland had broken down during work on The Blueprint 3, before they reunited.

Jay-Z also described a disagreement with Kanye West about which project should contain “Holy Grail” and “Oceans.” West wanted the tracks for Watch The Throne, while Jay-Z envisioned them on his own album.

Jay-Z said the disagreement over those two tracks lasted four days. He planned his solo album while he and West finished their joint project.

Apple’s host biography also describes Lowe as a working musician who continues to write, produce and record. That experience sits alongside his interviewing duties on The Zane Lowe Show and New Music Daily.

Lowe’s current home at Apple Music has built physical space around artist conversations. In June 2025, the company announced a Los Angeles facility covering more than 15,000 square feet across three floors.

Its plans included two radio studios that could accommodate interviews or impromptu performances, along with private booths for songwriting and one-on-one conversations. A separate 4,000-square-foot soundstage was designed for screenings, live shows and events with fans.

The Los Angeles site joined a wider studio network reaching cities including Nashville, Tokyo, Paris, Berlin and New York.

Apple Music Radio is available free worldwide, with programming running around the clock.

item.title: Rihanna Takes Jay-Z Collaboration “Talk That Talk” Double Platinum
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Rihanna adds four new RIAA awards, with her Jay-Z duet reaching two million units and its parent album earning more platinum.
item.content:encoded:
Rihanna has another platinum milestone with Jay-Z, as their “Talk That Talk” collaboration reaches double-platinum status, along with three other upgrades from the same album.

The title track’s award recognizes two million U.S. units. The Talk That Talk album itself is now four-times platinum, giving Rihanna another certification for the project that paired her with the Brooklyn rapper.

Billboard reported the upgrades alongside a new batch for Dua Lipa. Rihanna’s “Where Have You Been” advances to six-times platinum, while “You Da One” reaches four-times platinum.

World Music Views reports that all four Rihanna awards carry a November 17, 2026, certification date. The recognition covers three individual songs and the album that houses them.

Those totals combine purchases and eligible listening activity. Under the RIAA’s digital single rules, one permanent download or 150 on-demand audio or video streams counts as one unit.

Albums use a different calculation: one album purchase, 10 track downloads or 1,500 on-demand streams each count toward one album unit. Platinum begins at one million units, with additional levels awarded in million-unit increments.

The four awards return attention to Rihanna’s sixth studio album, released in 2011. It entered the Billboard 200 at No. 3, while its singles took different paths up the Hot 100.

“Where Have You Been” climbed to No. 5, “You Da One” reached No. 14 and the Jay-Z-assisted title track peaked at No. 31. The new plaques measure their accumulated U.S. consumption long after those chart runs.

The upgrades follow another catalog milestone earlier this year. Billboard reported that “Love on the Brain” became Rihanna’s eighth diamond single during ANTI‘s 10th-anniversary celebrations in January, extending her record for the most diamond singles by a female artist.

Another song from Talk That Talk had already crossed the diamond threshold. As AllHipHop reported in 2023, “We Found Love,” featuring Calvin Harris, reached 10 million units.

Rihanna performed that song during her Super Bowl LVII halftime show in Glendale, Arizona. It was part of a set that brought her catalog back onto one of television’s biggest stages.

“We Found Love” spent 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

item.title: Big Sean Keeps Detroit Entertainment Project In Motion
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Big Sean pursues another Detroit entertainment venture as his hometown creative push draws interest from Jocelyn Benson.
item.content:encoded:
Big Sean is still working on a Detroit entertainment project as Michigan’s incoming governor expresses interest in the effort.

The rapper’s plans aim to expand the city’s creative industry. His latest update comes as Detroit figures discuss opportunities to build more entertainment business at home.

Big Sean and Jalen Rose spoke on a panel about that subject, according to Crain’s Detroit Business. The outlet reported that Big Sean described a project intended to advance the entertainment industry.

The conversation follows his work with Jocelyn Benson during her campaign for governor.

In September, Big Sean joined artists, entrepreneurs and business leaders for a Detroit discussion about investment in creative work.

Benson’s campaign described a focus on helping Michigan keep talent and supporting people building businesses in creative fields. Big Sean connected that argument to the city’s industrial history, pointing to the invention behind its automotive success.

“The reason Detroit has ever been as big as it was is because it was funded by creativity,” Big Sean said at that gathering.

Benson also supported restoring film-production tax incentives and creating a state department covering arts, culture, tourism and sports. She said during the campaign that she wanted to establish that department through an executive order in her first month.

Big Sean has already helped finance places where younger Detroit residents can learn entertainment skills.

He and Usher committed $1 million to a creative incubator at Michigan Central, with programs spanning music, film and technology.

Plans for that facility included a virtual production studio, a special-effects lab and space for creators to work.

The partnership brought together their foundations, Ilitch Sports + Entertainment and Emory University’s Goizueta Business School.

The incubator’s planned programming served young people ages 14 to 24, pairing industry instruction with mentorship and opportunities to develop their own ventures.

Its curriculum extended into artificial intelligence, immersive technology and three-dimensional design. Participants could also earn credentials through the partners and seek startup funding for their businesses.

Big Sean’s foundation had previously helped establish four studios at Boys & Girls Club locations, providing access to music production and DJ equipment.

item.title: Litmus Music Secures $475M For More Catalog Acquisitions
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Litmus Music adds KKR backing as fresh capital expands the catalog buyer's reach across publishing and recorded music.
item.content:encoded:
Litmus Music is putting another $475 million behind its catalog-buying ambitions, adding KKR as an investor alongside longtime backer Carlyle.

The company already holds rights involving Juice WRLD, among other artists. Its new financing gives it more money to pursue additional catalogs, with Carlyle retaining majority ownership after the transaction.

In its announcement, Litmus described the money as capital commitments for acquisitions over the coming years. The firm has about $1.4 billion in assets under management, with a portfolio exceeding 100,000 copyrights and recordings.

“This investment marks an exciting next chapter for our company, providing meaningful additional capital to pursue new deals and accelerate growth,” CEO Hank Forsyth said.

Litmus’ connection to Juice WRLD predates this investment. In 2024, it bought Opus Music Group, whose holdings included rights associated with the late rapper, Maluma, Ozuna and Rauw Alejandro.

That purchase followed Opus’ earlier acquisition of a large stake in Juice WRLD’s catalog. Litmus financed the Opus transaction through a revolving credit facility that had been expanded to $400 million, according to reporting at the time.

The company had already bought compositions from benny blanco and rights tied to Katy Perry’s first five Capitol albums. Perry’s transaction covered her publishing and share of master royalty income, while Universal Music Group continued to own or control the recordings.

KKR brings its own history of buying into music. Its relationship with BMG dates to 2009, when it backed the company with 250 million euros to acquire publishing assets.

The two businesses joined forces again in 2021, with purchases involving music from John Legend and ZZ Top. KKR subsequently backed HarbourView Equity Partners through two $500 million asset-backed securitizations and bought European concert promoter Superstruct Entertainment.

Litmus also holds rights involving music by Randy Newman and Keith Urban.

Litmus’ founders also came through the record business. Forsyth worked at EMI, Warner Chappell and Blue Note, while co-founder Dan McCarroll led Capitol Records and later Warner Bros. Records.

Carlyle helped establish Litmus in 2022 with an initial $500 million commitment spanning equity and debt, alongside management’s investment.

KKR is funding its new investment primarily through its Asset-Based Finance Partners II fund.

item.title: YNW Melly Faces Prosecutors’ Challenge To Alibi Notice & Rap Evidence Motions
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: YNW Melly's pretrial calendar fills with fights over witnesses, digital records and attempts to exclude rap evidence.
item.content:encoded:
YNW Melly‘s alibi notice and effort to keep rap lyrics out of his murder retrial are headed for hearings as prosecutors ask a judge to strike several defense filings.

A two-page notice, electronically filed at 2:55 P.M. November 18 in Broward County, lays out seven matters the State plans to argue before Judge Martin Fein. Prosecutors are listed for November 20, 23 and 24, with hearings beginning at 9 A.M. in Courtroom 4780.

The agenda reaches beyond the gang-testimony dispute Melly’s attorneys raised last week. It also targets his supplemental witness list and a defense request to suppress material obtained through warrants involving an iPhone, Google, Snapchat and Instagram.

Those warrants were issued March 21, 2024, according to the notice, which appears in the Broward Clerk’s case records. The State identifies its requested action on that issue as striking the defense suppression motion.

Prosecutors also list a “Motion to Strike Defendant’s Alibi Notice” and a separate challenge to the supplemental witness list. The filing identifies the matters set for argument rather than presenting the State’s reasons for each request. The notice carries three prosecutors’ signatures.

The music-related dispute concerns the defense’s bid to exclude rap lyrics and videos. Another listed State motion challenges Melly’s effort to keep gang evidence and gang-expert testimony away from jurors.

Melly’s lawyers filed that gang-related request November 13. They argued that testimony at the first trial described alleged gang affiliations without connecting the material to the charged killings. Their eight-page filing focused on the risk that broad testimony about gang culture would prejudice jurors.

Timing-advance records are another contested category on the State’s hearing agenda. The docket shows a defense motion seeking their exclusion was also filed November 13.

A seventh matter concerns a State request to exclude testimony from Michelle Boutros and Kristine Bradley. The new notice dates that underlying motion to December 17, 2023.

Melly has pleaded not guilty to two first-degree murder charges stemming from the 2018 deaths of YNW Sakchaser and YNW Juvy. His first trial ended in a jury deadlock in July 2023.

The court’s hearing calendar lists his jury trial for January 6, 2027.

item.title: Suno Promises Artist-Likeness Filters As It Expands Into AI Music Videos
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Suno adds visual identity checks to its video push while Eminem's publishers pursue a separate fight over song copyrights.
item.content:encoded:
Suno is promising to keep artists’ faces out of unauthorized AI videos as it expands beyond music, with a copyright lawsuit from Eminem‘s publisher already on its plate.

The company introduced Visuals on November 17, allowing users to generate images and short videos around their songs.

In Suno’s announcement, chief product officer Jack Brody described filters intended to catch requests for depictions of specific performers, public figures and copyrighted material. Those checks cover both incoming prompts and uploads, the company says.

“This means that prompts that work on other video platforms may not work on Suno and that’s by design,” Brody wrote.

Suno says it also screens finished images and videos before users see them, adding outside tools to its own filters. Watermarks are supposed to travel with Visuals when users share them elsewhere.

The company’s musical output is already facing a different kind of challenge. As AllHipHop previously reported, Eight Mile Style and Martin Affiliated sued Suno over compositions from Eminem’s catalog.

Their November 6 complaint identifies 269 works and alleges Suno copied protected material without permission to develop its music-generation system. The publishers also accuse the service of producing lyrics and musical elements drawn from those compositions.

That case concerns songwriting copyrights, including the alleged use of songs during training and in generated output. The new Visuals announcement addresses another issue: whether a user can make an unauthorized image of a recognizable performer.

The complaint names the two publishing companies as plaintiffs and Suno as the defendant. Its allegations include copyright infringement, circumventing technological protections and removing copyright-management information.

Music Business Worldwide reported that Visuals runs on MiniMax’s H3 Move model. MiniMax is a Shanghai-based AI company listed in Hong Kong.

Among the songs named in the publishers’ complaint are “Stan,” “Lose Yourself” and “Without Me.” The companies say they control licensing rights to those works and never authorized their use for Suno’s training.

The publishers requested a jury trial in federal court in Northern California. Their complaint also asks for an injunction and an accounting of training data, scraping activities and datasets involving the compositions they say they control.
